title: Executive dashboard projectIds filter narrows results to only projects the caller can access
description: GET /organizations/:orgId/executive-dashboard runs filterAccessibleProjectIds on the requested projectIds before calling service.getDashboard, so a caller cannot widen scope by simply naming a project they don't have access to.
preconditions: User has access to projects P1 and P2 but not P3, all in the same org
expectedResult: The service is invoked with projectIds narrowed to [P1, P2] only; returned KPI data is scoped to P1+P2 and excludes any P3-only initiatives, risks, or evidence.

title: Risk heatmap short-circuits to an empty object when the caller has zero accessible projects in scope
description: executive-dashboard.routes.ts's risk-heatmap handler checks `if (!projectIds.length) return reply.send({ success: true, data: {} })` after filtering — verifies this early-exit path instead of falling through to service.getHeatMapDistribution with an empty filter (which could silently return org-wide data).
preconditions: User requests projectIds consisting only of a project they cannot access
expectedResult: Response is 200 { success: true, data: {} } — service.getHeatMapDistribution is never invoked, and no org-wide heatmap data is returned as an unintended fallback.

title: Compliance Oversight /summary degrades to the documented null-input shape when accessible projectIds is empty
description: When filterAccessibleProjectIds returns an empty array, the /summary handler returns buildSmartCompliance(null)/buildAuditAssurance(null,null,0)/etc. directly rather than calling CrossServiceIntegration with an empty filter.
preconditions: User requests projectIds consisting only of an inaccessible project
expectedResult: Response returns overallScore 0, activeFrameworks 0, empty upcomingAudits/recentActivities arrays — matching the exact all-null builder output — without any call to CrossServiceIntegration.fetchComplianceData/fetchEvidenceData and without throwing.

title: Vendor risk distribution normalizes correctly across all 3 vendor-service response shapes
description: buildRiskDistribution tries, in order: (1) dashboard's flat riskDistribution object, (2) analytics.data.vendorStats.byRiskTier nested path, (3) legacy [{risk,count}] array. Tier 1 must win when multiple tiers are simultaneously present, per applyFlatDistribution's early return on the first non-zero match.
preconditions: vendor-service dashboard/analytics responses can be mocked in 3 shapes: flat, nested vendorStats.byRiskTier, and legacy array
steps: Mock vendor-service to return only the legacy array format; call GET /third-party-risk/summary and record the riskDistribution
Mock vendor-service to return only the nested vendorStats.byRiskTier format; repeat
Mock vendor-service to return both a flat riskDistribution AND a conflicting nested vendorStats.byRiskTier; repeat
expectedResult: All 3 individual-format calls produce an identical {critical,high,medium,low} shape with correct counts; the mixed-format call in step 3 uses the flat riskDistribution values (tier 1), ignoring the conflicting nested tier.

title: Report download falls back to direct PDF streaming when S3 is unavailable
description: GET /reports/:reportId/download: when reportingService.getDownloadUrl returns statusCode 404 or 503 (no S3 presigned URL configured/stored), the route falls back to generatorService.generateReportForStream and streams the regenerated PDF bytes directly instead of erroring.
preconditions: A generated report exists with no S3-backed file (S3 service disabled or getDownloadUrl configured to return 503)
expectedResult: Response streams the regenerated PDF with Content-Type application/pdf, a sanitized Content-Disposition filename, correct Content-Length, and Cache-Control: no-store — the user receives a usable file rather than a 500/404.

title: Initiative creation rejects a timeline where targetDate precedes startDate
description: CreateInitiativeSchema's .refine() on the timeline object enforces targetDate > startDate at the Zod layer before the route even calls service.createInitiative.
steps: POST /initiatives with timeline.startDate = 2026-09-01 and timeline.targetDate = 2026-08-01, otherwise valid body
expectedResult: 400 response with error path timeline.targetDate and message 'Target date must be after start date'; no initiative document is persisted.

title: FAIR scenario creation rejects a malformed projectId before invoking the service layer
description: POST /scenarios checks ObjectId.isValid(request.body.projectId) inline in the route handler and returns 400 'Invalid projectId' before service.createScenario is ever called.
steps: POST /scenarios with projectId: 'not-an-object-id' and otherwise valid lossEventFrequency/lossMagnitude ranges
expectedResult: 400 'Invalid projectId' is returned; RiskIntelligenceService.createScenario is never invoked and no draft scenario document is created.

title: Advisor message send surfaces a timeout without losing the user's already-persisted message
description: The route persists the user message (step 3, saveMessage) before calling python-ai (step 4). If callPythonAI's AbortController fires after AI_TIMEOUT_MS, the route returns 504/502 — verifies the earlier user message survives this failure and is visible on retry, while no assistant message is written for the failed turn.
preconditions: python-ai service is unreachable or configured to exceed AI_TIMEOUT_MS for this request
steps: POST /conversations/:id/messages with a valid content string while python-ai is unresponsive
Inspect the response and then GET /conversations/:id/messages
expectedResult: The POST returns 504 'AI service timed out' or 502/503 'AI service error'/'AI service temporarily unavailable'; the subsequent GET shows the user's message persisted in history with no corresponding assistant message for that turn.
